title: the OC Hypercar's super ultra 4K HD pass, matched to the owner's four references, outside and cockpit
lensAText: FIRST open the owner's four new references with the Read tool (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Claude/104ede24-b5bc-5131-bb4c-1bc7e86a4fd2/scratchpad/owner/hypercar-refs-2026-11-15/front34.png, side.png, rear34.png, interior.png): they govern. Compare the builder's side-by-side images and your own matching frames: how close is our car to each (shape, nose and fins, bonnet louvres, side triangle intake, light lines, rear blades, honeycomb, twin exhausts, diffuser fins, wing, snorkel; and the cockpit: Alcantara, carbon, white bolsters, blue stitching, ambient lines, hex wheel, cluster, round dials, portrait screen, toggles)? Name the biggest remaining differences. Then: a sceptical automotive art director for a premium driving game. Look at every before/after image the builder cites with the Read tool and at the owner's wheel references (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Claude/104ede24-b5bc-5131-bb4c-1bc7e86a4fd2/scratchpad/owner/hyper-wheel/wheel-ref-1.webp, -2, -3), then build dist/artifact.html yourself and take your own frames in ONE short Playwright script: the OC Hypercar from the chase and hood cameras on the freeway by day and at night (1280x720), the seat view (setCam('cockpit')) at 390x844 (phone viewport copy, isMobile, hasTouch, DPR 3) and 1280x720 by day and night, and the garage view. Also judge the owner's later asks: does Ultra render natively up to 4K with crisp 2048-4096 px surface detail (check the builder's 3840x2160 renders and 100 % crops), does the wheel match the owner's three pictures closely (only the emblem differs), and is the cockpit futuristic and rich (layered surfaces, floating glass displays with real data, ice-blue ambient lines, hex motifs, perforated Alcantara, lit console switches, a subtle HUD reflection) rather than plain? Judge: is the outside now a clear step up (clean deep paint with unbroken reflections and no dark patches or faceting, deliberate two-tone edges, shut lines, carbon weave, crisp lights, grounded by a contact shadow, the same silhouette)? Is the cockpit a premium hypercar interior with a clearer view of the road (slimmer pillars, sculpted fender tops, Alcantara and stitching, carbon, ambient lines), and does the wheel follow the owner's references (navy Alcantara with blue stitching, carbon sections, silver spokes, rounded-hex centre, lit 12 o'clock line) while keeping the OC mark? Our own design, no real brand marks, no emblem from the reference pictures? Are the other four cars unchanged? Drive 60 s in the seat view steering to full lock both ways at 390x844 DPR 3 and watch for clipping, z-fighting, flicker, shimmer or stutter; check the builder's frame-time table against one short measurement of your own (CDP CPU throttle 4).
brief: NEW OWNER REFERENCES, THEY GOVERN (2026-11-15 ~3:55 PM PT, the owner: "Use these images from ChatGPT to use as references and keep rendering"): four 1672x941 renders of the OC Hypercar: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Claude/104ede24-b5bc-5131-bb4c-1bc7e86a4fd2/scratchpad/owner/hypercar-refs-2026-11-15/front34.png, /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Claude/104ede24-b5bc-5131-bb4c-1bc7e86a4fd2/scratchpad/owner/hypercar-refs-2026-11-15/side.png, /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Claude/104ede24-b5bc-5131-bb4c-1bc7e86a4fd2/scratchpad/owner/hypercar-refs-2026-11-15/rear34.png and /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Claude/104ede24-b5bc-5131-bb4c-1bc7e86a4fd2/scratchpad/owner/hypercar-refs-2026-11-15/interior.png. Open all four with the Read tool FIRST and match them AS CLOSELY AS the real-time procedural model allows; they supersede the lost sheet where they differ, and the silhouette may now move toward them (this is no longer 'graphics only'). Note what they show and build it: OUTSIDE: pearl-white/silver paint with fine flake; a dark tinted canopy with a roof snorkel scoop; mirrors on slim stalks; a sharp V nose with thin ice-blue LED blades rising along the front fender edges; a large black vented louvre panel on the bonnet; an aggressive carbon front with many vertical fins over a dark honeycomb-mesh intake and a deep carbon splitter outlined by a thin ice-blue light line; the big dark TRIANGULAR side intake behind the door filled with honeycomb mesh; thin ice-blue light lines along the sills and the side skirt; black fender vents behind the front wheels; at the rear two slim ice-blue tail-light blades at the top of the tail, a honeycomb-mesh rear panel, centred twin round exhausts, a deep carbon diffuser with five tall vertical fins, a large carbon wing on two uprights with big end plates; carbon fibre with a visible weave on the splitter, fins, diffuser, wing and mirrors; black multi-spoke wheels with blue calipers (the wheels are car-wheel.ts, another session's file: do not edit it; if the wheel or caliper look needs a change there, list it for that session). INSIDE (interior.png): black Alcantara dash and tub with blue stitching; carbon fibre trim with visible weave; thin ice-blue ambient light lines along the dash, doors and console; white leather side bolsters on the seats with blue stitching; door cards in carbon and Alcantara with white accents; a flat-bottomed wheel with a hex-shaped centre pad, carbon lower spoke, blue 12 o'clock stripe and silver paddles (keep our OC mark on the centre; the wheel refs from Nov 11 agree); a wide digital cluster (speed, gear, side bars) behind the wheel; three round knurled dials on the centre stack; a tall portrait touchscreen in the console (showing REAL game data only: the map/next turn, the car's tune, Thrust; never fuel or other values the game does not simulate, even though the reference cluster shows a fuel icon); a row of toggle switches and a start/gear button below it; alloy pedals; a rear-view mirror. Prove the match with side-by-side images: each of the four references beside our render from the same camera (garage/test-car.ts cameras for the outside, the seat view for the inside), at Ultra, 1672x941. THE OWNER ADDED (2026-11-15 ~3:30 PM PT): "Like to make it super ultra 4k hd. Use the images I already provided to render as close as possible. Interior cockpit needs to look more HD and futuristic and not plain and simple." So, on top of everything below: (I) SUPER ULTRA 4K HD on the ULTRA tier (HD gets most of it where cheap; Low stays cheap): render at the screen's native resolution up to 4K on desktop Ultra (raise the pixel-ratio cap for Ultra so a 3840x2160 screen renders natively; phones keep a DPR cap that holds the frame rate, stated); the hypercar's surface detail generated at RUNTIME as procedural canvases (no file-size cost in the single-file build) at 2048-4096 px on Ultra, 1024 on HD, 256-512 on Low: paint metallic-flake normal map, carbon weave (normal + roughness) under clear coat, Alcantara nap, leather grain, stitching, brushed/machined metal streaks, shut-line maps; maximum anisotropy and mipmaps on all of them; anti-aliasing on Ultra (MSAA or SMAA/FXAA, whichever the renderer path supports without breaking the post chain); HDR environment reflections (PMREM of the sky, a studio key in the garage) so the paint and glass look real. Generate the big canvases once (cached, disposed on quality change), never per frame; state the memory cost. (II) AS CLOSE AS POSSIBLE TO THE OWNER'S IMAGES: the steering wheel must match the owner's three wheel pictures closely (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Claude/104ede24-b5bc-5131-bb4c-1bc7e86a4fd2/scratchpad/owner/hyper-wheel/wheel-ref-1.webp, -2, -3) in shape, materials, colours, stitching, lit lines, spokes, touch panels and rollers (only the emblem differs: keep the OC mark), proven with side-by-side crops; the exterior keeps the reference sheet's design as recorded in PROJECT_OC_HYPERCAR.md (the sheet itself was lost in a reset; if the owner re-sends it, a match pass follows). (III) A FUTURISTIC, HD COCKPIT, NOT PLAIN: layered sculpted surfaces instead of flat panels; floating glass display panels with emissive edges (the cluster and a centre screen showing REAL game data only: the map/next turn, the Thrust tank, the tune, the clock 'sim'); ice-blue ambient light strips tracing the dash, door and console contours (a soft glow that reads at night, subtle by day); hexagonal motifs echoing the wheel's centre; a carbon tub with visible weave; perforated Alcantara on the seat bolsters and door cards; an illuminated centre tunnel with guarded toggle switches and a lit start button; a subtle head-up display reflection on the windshield showing speed and the next turn (real data, readable, not covering the road); thin satin-silver trim lines; all in the wheel references' palette (navy, ice blue, carbon black, satin silver). Keep the view of the road clear (slimmer pillars) and keep it smooth on phones (Low gets a simpler cockpit). PROOF additions: 3840x2160 renders on Ultra of the hero, the rear 3/4 and the seat view, each with a 100 % crop showing the texture detail; the wheel beside each of the owner's three pictures; day and night cockpit frames on Low, HD and Ultra at 1280x720 and 390x844. THE OWNER (2026-11-15 ~3:25 PM PT): "let's also start fixing the graphics for the OC hyper car both outside and inside the car" (and earlier, Nov 11: "make sure graphics are insane for both the steering wheel and characters and ... no laggy graphics or glitchy 1st person POV"). HEAD is 572111a (origin/claude/sport-wheel: the live v15 game plus the reviewed dashboard and wheel centre, which go live in drop 3 tonight); branch claude/hyper-gfx. Read PROJECT_OC_HYPERCAR.md (the M1/M1b/M2 notes: the body is a procedural model in src/preview/car-shape.ts, car-body.ts, car-kit.ts, car-mats.ts, car-tex.ts, car.ts, oc-mark.ts; the cockpit in src/preview/cockpit.ts, wheel-sport.ts, car-dash.ts; the game wiring in src/game/vehicle/PlayerCar.ts) and PROJECT_OC_STYLE_GUIDE.md first. The owner's reference sheet (scratchpad/ref/hypercar-reference.png) was lost in a machine reset; use the figures recorded in PROJECT_OC_HYPERCAR.md and the M1b renders as the shape to keep (this is a GRAPHICS pass, not a redesign: same silhouette and proportions). (A) OUTSIDE (garage, chase, hood and hero cameras): make it read as a premium real-time hypercar: (1) paint: a deep clear-coat silver with fine metallic flake and crisp, unbroken reflections (fix the stretched dark patches and blotches on the bonnet and front fenders seen in M1b's hero, whose cause was never traced; no faceting: smooth normals or more stations where needed); (2) the two-tone: the gloss-black areas with clean, deliberate edges (no ragged patches or blotchy masks; the side triangles and fender scoops should read as designed shapes); (3) shut lines and panel gaps (doors, bonnet, engine cover) as thin dark lines; (4) carbon fibre with a visible weave under clear coat on the splitter, diffuser, side blades, wing and mirrors; (5) the glass/canopy dark tinted with real reflections; (6) lights: the headlamp blades and the rear bar crisp and emissive with a subtle bloom on HD/Ultra, LED detail in the lamp sockets; (7) underbody contact shadow / ambient occlusion so it sits on the road; (8) a few hero details: mesh grilles in the intakes, the exhaust exits, a fine aero vane set in the diffuser, mirror stalks. The road wheels' rims, tyres and calipers live in src/preview/car-wheel.ts, which another session owns: do NOT edit it; you may change only how the car's own materials are passed to it if that is already a public option. (B) INSIDE (the seat view the player drives in, phone 390x844 and desktop): today the view shows a huge black diagonal A-pillar/canopy frame over the top-left, plain grey fender humps over the dash, flat featureless dash and door panels and a blank grey console. Make it a premium hypercar cockpit, keeping the player's view of the road clear: slimmer A-pillars and canopy frame (or a frame that reads as sculpted carbon, not a black slab) that hide less of the road; the fender tops seen over the dash as sculpted silver forms with clean reflections; the dash top in navy Alcantara with blue double stitching; a carbon tub and centre console with satin-silver trim lines, gloss-black touch panels with thin icons, ice-blue ambient light lines; sculpted door cards; the mirror housings in carbon. THE WHEEL (owner's references, Nov 11: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Claude/104ede24-b5bc-5131-bb4c-1bc7e86a4fd2/scratchpad/owner/hyper-wheel/wheel-ref-1.webp, -2, -3: look at them): deep navy Alcantara grips with bright blue double stitching, gloss carbon top and bottom sections with thin silver trim lines, a lit ice-blue line at 12 o'clock and down the lower spoke, satin silver/titanium sculpted spokes and paddles, a rounded-hexagon centre in navy leather/Alcantara with a blue stitched edge, gloss-black touch panels with thin icons and small knurled metal rollers on the upper spokes; keep the hub lane's centre structure and badge cup; the badge stays the current OC mark (the owner's new emblems are not picked yet; the emblems drawn in those pictures must NOT be used); the rim path and grips where the hands hold it (GRIP 32/148 deg) unchanged; the dials, thumb pads, paddles, shift lights and the new cluster keep working. RULES: our own design only (no real brand's logo, name or copied shape); the other four cars (Rossini GT, Corsa, Brio, Vela E) must be UNCHANGED: hash their geometry and material settings against HEAD as M1b did (tests/out/preview/m1b/hash/) and show pixel-identical renders; do NOT edit src/preview/spec.ts, hands*, car-wheel.ts, Physics.ts, src/onfoot/*; Low stays cheap for phones (simpler interior and materials on Low), HD and Ultra get the full detail; stay inside the hypercar's budget in PROJECT_OC_HYPERCAR.md section 10 (40 draw calls / 260,000 triangles high, 36 / 135,000 phone) unless a small, stated increase on HD/Ultra buys a visible step (never on Low); no per-frame allocation; mipmaps and anisotropy on every new texture (no shimmer); no z-fighting or flicker. SMOOTHNESS: measure a 60 s seat-view drive with steering to full lock both ways, phone profile (390x844, DPR 3, isMobile, CDP CPU throttle 4) and desktop 1280x720, as 3 alternating base/ours pairs (base = a clean build of 572111a in a temporary detached worktree under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Claude/104ede24-b5bc-5131-bb4c-1bc7e86a4fd2/scratchpad/tmp-base, node_modules symlinked from /home/user/Claude/tsu-live/top-speed-ultra/node_modules, removed afterwards); PASS = draw calls and triangles within the stated budget, median p50 within +10 %, median p95 within +10 % or inside the base's own spread, no heap growth. PROVE: npx tsc --noEmit (both configs); npm run build (one owner-test mark); npm test -- --only=boot,phone,render (each run under 20 minutes; split render with --check if needed); before (572111a) and after renders into tests/out/hyper-gfx/: test-car.ts views hero (the sheet's camera), hero-night, front, rear, rear 3/4, side, top, wheel close-up and the interior/seat view, plus in-game frames: chase and hood on the freeway by day and at night (1280x720), and the seat view at 390x844 (phone viewport copy, DPR 3) and 1280x720, day and night; a close-up of the steering wheel beside the owner's three wheel references. Look at every image you cite. Log it in PROJECT_OC_HYPERCAR.md (a new 'G1 graphics pass' row) and PROJECT_OC_PROGRESS.md.

commit.subject: The OC Hypercar's super ultra 4K HD graphics pass, outside and a futuristic cockpit
commit.how: The branch claude/hyper-gfx is new (no upstream yet), cut from 572111a (origin/claude/sport-wheel). Push with 'git push -u origin claude/hyper-gfx'.
